body:
## Problem

The quick gate compares the worktree against the local `main` branch. In this repository, agents do not pull in the main checkout while a gate runs (#1201). Thus the local `main` can be many commits behind `origin/main`.

When the base is stale, the diff holds many files that the branch did not change. The quick gate then falls back to the batch plan.

## Seen

On the branch of PR #3738, the local `main` was `d66400b78`. The diff against it had 2056 files. The quick gate fell back to batch. The change itself touched only `xtask/`.

## Expected

The quick gate uses the merge base with `origin/main` (after `git fetch`), or it warns when the local `main` is behind `origin/main`.

## Notes

- `gate heavy --base main` can have the same problem.
- A test must pin the choice of the base.

body:
﻿The Ooznest WorkBee of #3038 runs Estlcam's own control software. No built-in post is confirmed to write programs that this control accepts. The machine file of #3038 names no post for this reason.

Estlcam publishes its rules for programs from other CAM programs: https://www.estlcam.de/steuerung_cnc_programme.php. The rules include:
- Only G00, G01, G02 and G03 run. The control ignores each other G word with no message.
- Each motion line must have its own G word. Modal output (a line with no G word) is not permitted.
- One G word and one M word for each line. The control ignores later words on the line.
- No cycles, subprograms, variables or expressions.
- G02/G03 use I/J only (no R), relative to the start point, in the XY plane only. No full circles. A helix is permitted.
- Absolute coordinates only. No work offset change.
- The length and feed units are set in Estlcam. G20/G21 have no effect.
- M words: M00, M01, M03, M05, M06, M08, M09, M10, M11. The control ignores other M words.
- Comments in parentheses. UTF-8 or ASCII.

Work:
- A built-in post `Estlcam` (or a `.cps`) that writes only these words. It must split a full circle into two arcs and expand drill cycles into G00/G01 moves, or refuse them by name.
- Conformance goldens for a 2D profile and a drill.
- Name the post in `assets/machines/ooznest-workbee-1000x1500.mch` (`controller.post`).

Done means: a 2D contour posts for the WorkBee with each line in Estlcam's rules, pinned by goldens.

body:
The maintainer asked for this change on 2026-11-23: "Do your changes as a docs changes, push it and merge it and announce it one go.. On my call."

What the data shows (30 PRs, 2026-11-20 to 2026-11-23, 36 times a ready PR went back to draft):
- 27 of 36 followed a `needs-rework` label. 17 came from our own reviews and 10 from the author's reviewer.
- 3 followed a `conflicts` label. 6 had no label cause.
- The median time from ready to draft is 1.6 hours.
- #3283 and #3284 flipped three times each. #3061 returned four times for one class of defect.

Each round trip costs one more read and one more trial.

The change:
1. A `needs-rework` finding does not turn a ready PR back into a draft. The author pushes the fix to the same PR. A push moves the head, so the earlier review and `merge-ready` do not count for the new head.
2. An orange `conflicts` verdict still makes one of our own PRs a draft.
3. The first `needs-rework` comment names the class of each finding and asks for one rule that closes the class.

Done means: AGENTS.md, the `review-prs` skill and the `resolve-conflicts` skill say this, a decision file records the maintainer's order, and PROCESS_VERSION is bumped and announced on #681.

title: Verifier: decide whether a named over-deep dive stands as a proven floor for the later laws

labels.name: question

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P8
labels.description: Larger idea needing design or research before code

body:
Found while working #3679.

## What happens

`Rest::cut` takes the chords of every non-Rapid move. A feed dive that
the plunge depth law names (`PlungeTooDeep`, #3679) inserts its own
chord into that set. A later move then reads the dive's column as
cleared to the dive bottom:

- `crates/sim/tests/plunge_depth.rs`, test
  `a_feed_plunge_deeper_than_one_stepdown_below_uncut_stock_is_named`,
  pins this: the re-entry plunge after the 18 mm dive reads the column
  as cleared to Z -18 and stays clean.

The rest model is physically true: the dive removed that material,
unsafely, but it did remove it. The question is whether a verifier
should treat an unsafe removal as a proven floor, or should exclude a
named dive from the clearing set so the later laws speak against the
stock that should still stand.

## Expected

A recorded decision: keep the current reading, or exclude over-deep
dives from `Rest::cut`. Each answer gets its own pinning test.

## Done means

A `docs/decisions/` entry names the choice, and the verify tests pin
the chosen reading.

## Notes

- #3678 fixes the generator dives. After it, no tab window dive is
  over-deep, so the question matters only for hand-built or imported
  programs.

title: Post-merge gate: drop superseded queued runs when merges arrive in bursts

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

body:
**Proposal, for the maintainer to decide.** It changes the one-run-per-commit design of #3184, so it is not a defect.

What happens: when several PRs merge within minutes, each push queues its own post-merge run. All of them wait for the `camcraft-post-merge` runners. On 2026-11-23 between 14:08 and 14:29 UTC, five runs were open at once (`33685374f`, `f81bcac8c`, `77c655fb7`, `5427b4872`, `dac6a896b`). Three were cancelled by hand, and a merge after that made the newest one obsolete too. A green run on a later commit already covers the earlier ones, so a run still queued behind a newer queued run only adds runner time.

Proposal: keep #3184 for runs that have **started** (never cancel in progress, so a red run still names its own commit), and let GitHub drop runs that are still **queued** when a newer push queues:

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: post-merge-gate
  cancel-in-progress: false   # a running run always finishes
```

With one shared group, GitHub keeps one running and one pending run, and a newer push replaces the pending one. The trade-off: with several runners, runs no longer go in parallel (one at a time), and a red run can then cover more than one commit, so the cause has to be found by bisecting. On 2026-11-23 a local bisect of `first_router_part` took about 15 minutes (#3693).

A variant that keeps the parallel runners: a small step at the start of the gate job that exits green with a notice ("superseded by <sha>") when a newer push to main already has a queued or running post-merge run, like `post-merge-skip.sh` does for a cut.

Done means: the maintainer chooses one of the two (or neither), and post-merge.yml carries it with a comment naming this issue.

body:
Split from #3186. PR for #3186 does the asset selection, the catalog check and `plan::may_run_ignored` for directory suites. This issue holds the `quick.rs` part.

Today `quick.rs` runs the whole binary of a directory suite in these cases:

- `map_modules` (`xtask/src/quick.rs` about line 181) joins the Gate maps of all the module files of a suite. A src change selects the whole binary.
- A change outside the `#[test]` fns of one submodule sets `p.whole` (`quick.rs` about lines 103-133).

Change `quick.rs`:

1. Match each Gate map for each source file (`suites::Source`), not for the joined text.
2. When only some submodules match, or when one submodule changes outside its test fns, pass a libtest module filter: `--test <suite> <submod>::`.
3. Run the whole binary only when `main.rs` or a shared module changes.

This needs a new pick kind (a module filter for each binary) in `Picks`, in `describe` and in `steps`.

Done means: `xtask` unit tests show that a change in one submodule of a directory suite plans `--test <suite> <submod>::`, and that a change in `main.rs` plans the whole binary.

A second item from the #3186 work: `may_run_ignored` keeps the old rule for a flat suite. A `mod x;` line makes a flat suite heavy. About 175 flat suites with `mod common;` and no `#[ignore]` in their files get a heavy step at the cut (measured with `cargo xtask gate release --dry-run`). A walk of `suites::sources` for flat suites too removes these steps. Do this only with a review of the cut plan.

Part of #919.

labels.name: enhancement

labels.name: P8

body:
What happens:
A 2D Adaptive operation can have rest machining (#1446) and "Do not touch" (#3346) at the same time. No planner handles the combination.

The combination is reachable:
- `do_not_touch_applies(OpType::Adaptive2D)` is true (`crates/app/src/operation/types/avoid.rs`).
- `validate_do_not_touch` does not refuse a rest operation (`crates/app/src/commands/operation/do_not_touch.rs`).

The two planners do not compose:
- `adaptive_spiral_avoid_on` and `adaptive_trochoidal_avoid` take an `AvoidSpec` and no `RestParams`.
- `rest_adaptive_previous` takes `RestParams` and the prior stock and no keep-out.

What #3656 does now (decision, option A):
- The rest branch has precedence in the adaptive planner (`crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`).
- The rest planner plans the rest path. `verify_avoid` then checks the path. A hit is `Warning::AvoidHit`, and `blocks_post()` is true. So the post is blocked.
- This is a feature gap, not a wrong answer. A rest pass with a protected item can be blocked at post instead of planned clear.

Done means:
A planner or a named refusal handles the combination. The rest pass keeps the full tool clear of each protected item. Or the operation refuses by name at generation, before it plans.

Found while resolving the conflicts of #3656. Refs #3346, #1446.

**What happens**

haas.cps writes an F word with no decimal point. In mm, `ff()` writes every feed as a whole number: it returns `String(Math.round(v))` (assets/posts/haas.cps, function `ff`). In inch, `trimNum()` removes the point from a whole value, so 50.8 mm/min posts as `F2`.

```
G18 G3 X15. Y0. Z0. I-5. K0. F600
```

**Why it is wrong**

On a Haas mill, Setting 77 (Scale Integer F) sets how the control reads an F word that has no decimal point. Source: Haas Mill Operator's Manual 96-8000 rev V (January 2009), Settings, "77 - Scale Integer F". In mm at the DEFAULT value (.001), F1 is F.001, so F600 is 0.6 mm/min. At INTEGER, F600 is 600 mm/min. The manual says: "It is recommended that programmers always use a decimal point."

The post cannot know Setting 77 on the machine. With a decimal point, the control reads the same feed at all values of Setting 77.

#1836 fixed the same problem for the length words: `pt()` adds the point. `ff()` does not use `pt()`.

**What should happen**

Every F word that haas.cps writes has a decimal point, for example `F600.`, `F23.62` and `F2.`.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Post a mill operation in mm with the Haas post, or open crates/app/tests/golden/nc/haas/arc_planes.nc.
2. Look at the F words. They are `F600`, not `F600.`.

Version: main 8c6b77f94 (v0.25.0-519). Linux.

**Done means**

- `ff()` always writes a decimal point, in mm and in inch.
- The Haas goldens show `F600.` and the other feeds with a point.

Fixture: `crates/motion/tests/contour_tab_entry.rs` (L-shape 40 x 40 with a 25 x 25 notch, Outside, `bottom_z` -18.3, stepdown 4.5, 4 tabs 10 x 3, tool D6, Plunge entry, Arc lead r3, clearance 25, retract 12). "Floor" is the lowest level pass whose swept disc holds the point. "Disc floor" is the highest floor under the full tool disc.

Before #3453 (origin/main 44c13a01d), PLANAR links:

| level | window | entry XY | plunge Z | floor under centre | disc floor | below disc floor | crescent |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| -18 | 0 | (46.000, 8.865) | 2 -> -18 | -15.3 | 0 | 18.0 | 2.501 |
| -18 | 1 | (10.153, -6.000) | 12 -> -18 | -15.3 | 0 | 18.0 | 2.501 |
| -18 | 2 | (-6.000, 29.525) | 12 -> -18 | -15.3 | 0 | 18.0 | 2.501 |
| -18 | 3 | (21.000, 30.029) | 12 -> -18 | -15.3 | 0 | 18.0 | 2.501 |

After the #3453 PR (window 0 enters at the untabbed start; the tab layout ends the tabs on the spacing marks from the start), PLANAR links:

| level | window | entry XY | plunge Z | floor under centre | disc floor | below disc floor | crescent |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| -18 | 0 | (43.514, -5.802) | 2 -> -18 | -15.3 | -15.3 | 2.7 | 0 |
| -18 | 1 | (-5.165, -4.266) | 12 -> -18 | 0 | 0 | 18.0 | full disc |
| -18 | 2 | (-4.796, 44.676) | 12 -> -18 | 0 | 0 | 18.0 | full disc |
| -18 | 3 | (18.186, 19.500) | 12 -> -18 | -15.3 | -15.3 | 2.7 | 0 |

With the stay-down ramp preset (`level: KeepDown`, `transition: Ramp`), the untabbed levels below the first do not cut the lead-in. After #3453, window 0 of the -18 level plunges 2 -> -18 at (43.514, -5.802) with the disc floor at -4.5: 13.5 mm below the floor.

With Lead None, each window dive is on the ring, in the kerf of the level above: 2.7 mm below the floor. That case is correct.

## Expected

No feed plunge of a contour goes deeper than one stepdown below the floor that the levels above left under the full tool disc at that XY.

## Proposed fix (from #3453)

- A guard on the wall-side graze dive (`contour_step.rs` `graze`) and the tab-window dive (`contour.rs`, window `k > 0`), for each level below the first level of its ring.
- Read the floor under the full disc from the moves that the builder has posted (flat feed passes and plunge columns).
- If the dive goes deeper than one stepdown below that floor, peck: plunge one stepdown, rapid up, plunge the next step. Say it in one note.
- The uncut floor is `min(entry top, first ring level + stepdown)`, so a first level and the shelf bands do not change.
- An alternative is to cut the window lead-ins on the levels above. Compare the two.

Done means: `crates/motion/tests/contour_tab_entry.rs` asserts that every descent of the three presets is at most one stepdown below the disc floor, and the pinned window 1 and 2 readings change to that.

body:
## Summary

This issue proposes a new design for the tool library. It is a proposal for discussion. It contains no code.

The "Tool library" tab on the right side becomes one dialog. The **Tools** cell of the ribbon opens it. The dialog has two kinds of item: tools and holders. Each kind has a list, a rail and an editor with a large drawing.

### Pictures

**1. Tool list** (Document, My library, Catalog; categories on the left)
![Tool list](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/1acd3beb0b0e9378b06074e3e2615ba7cd5d89f4/tool-library-proposal/1-tool-list.png)

**2. Tool editor** (the list is a rail; parameters, the assembly group and the drawing)
![Tool editor](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/1acd3beb0b0e9378b06074e3e2615ba7cd5d89f4/tool-library-proposal/2-tool-editor.png)

**3. Recipes tab**
![Recipes tab](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/1acd3beb0b0e9378b06074e3e2615ba7cd5d89f4/tool-library-proposal/3-recipes.png)

**4. Holder list**
![Holder list](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/1acd3beb0b0e9378b06074e3e2615ba7cd5d89f4/tool-library-proposal/4-holder-list.png)

**5. Holder editor**
![Holder editor](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/1acd3beb0b0e9378b06074e3e2615ba7cd5d89f4/tool-library-proposal/5-holder-editor.png)

Interactive mock-up (one HTML file, no network access; download it and open it in a browser): https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/blob/1acd3beb0b0e9378b06074e3e2615ba7cd5d89f4/tool-library-proposal/mockup.html

## What we have today

- "Tool library" is a tab beside Properties (`tool_library::draw`). It lists the built-in catalog with an "Add" button.
- A tool is edited on a property page with four folded groups: Geometry, Holder, Cutting data and Catalog (`tool_settings_grid::grid`).
- The holder is a combo box inside the tool (`tool_holder_picker`). The holder library is built in (`holder_library.rs`).
- The tool drawing is a 260 px square (`tool_preview::draw`).
- The cutting data of a tool is a table of `CuttingRow` entries, one for each work material.

## The proposal

### 1. One dialog, opened from the ribbon

- The **Tools** cell of the ribbon opens the dialog. The tab on the right side goes away.
- The header has a switch: **Tools | Holders**.
- The first screen is a list. Categories are on the left. Items are on the right.
- A click on an item opens its editor. The list folds into a narrow rail on the left. The user can go from item to item in the rail. An arrow goes back to the full list.

### 2. Tools

- The list has three sources: Document, My library and Catalog.
- Each row shows: a small drawing, the T number, the name, the type, the diameter, the flute length, the number of flutes, the holder, the gauge length and the number of recipes.
- The editor has three tabs: **Tool**, **Recipes** and **Details**.
- The parameters are on the left. The drawing is on the right.

### 3. Holders are first-class items

- Holders have their own list. The list is grouped by spindle taper.
- Each row shows: the name, the taper, the clamp, the clamping range, the gauge length, the largest diameter and the number of tools that use the holder.
- A holder has its own editor: the machine side (taper), the tool side (clamp and clamping range) and the shape.
- The holder editor lists the tools that use the holder. A change to the holder updates each of these tools in one undo step.
- The list shows which taper the mounted machine takes. The holder picker of a tool marks the holders with a different taper.

### 4. One home for each field

Today some values are in two places. The proposal gives each value one owner:

| Owner | Fields |
|---|---|
| Tool | Cutter (diameter, flute length, corner radius, angles, flutes, helix, tool material) and shank diameter |
| Holder | Taper, clamp, clamping range, gauge length of the holder, largest diameter, shape |
| Assembly (tool in holder) | The holder that the tool uses, and the stick-out |

- The assembly is one boxed group at the bottom of the Tool tab.
- The gauge length of the assembly is not typed. The dialog shows it: holder gauge length + stick-out.
- The same group shows if the shank diameter is in the clamping range of the holder.
- A link in the group opens the holder in its editor.

### 5. A large drawing

- The drawing is to scale, from the tool tip to the spindle nose.
- It shows the cutter, the shank and the holder.
- It shows dimension lines: diameter, flute length, stick-out, gauge length and shank diameter.
- It shows the flutes as helix lines, from `flutes` and `helix_deg`. This is decoration only. It adds no geometry law.
- The user can switch off the dimensions, the holder and the flutes.
- The drawing changes when the user changes a value.

### 6. Recipes

- The **Recipes** tab shows one row for each work material: spindle speed, feed, stepdown and stepover.
- Below each row the dialog shows the surface speed and the feed per tooth.
- A mark shows the row of the work material of the document. Operations use that row.
- Buttons: "Add material", "Suggest feeds and speeds" and "Copy recipes from tool".
- The data is the `CuttingRow` table of today. Plasma and waterjet tools keep their own recipe columns.

## What does not change

- Each Apply is one undoable command: `AddTool`, `ChangeTool`, `SetToolBody`, `ApplyCuttingData`. The MCP tools stay as they are.
- The file formats (`.camtools`, PathPilot `.csv`, Hurco `.TCM`) stay as they are.
- The page tests `layout_page_tool` and `layout_page_tool_library` need a new home as `layout_window_*` tests.

## Relation to open issues

- #3645 (user library store): "My library" needs it. This dialog is its front end.
- #3648 (component library browser) and #808 (holder library follow-ups): the Holders list and editor.
- #2452 and #3642 to #3647 (component-based tool assemblies, ISO 13399): a tool, a holder and a stick-out are the smallest assembly. The assembly group can grow into the assembly editor (extensions, inserts).
- #3393 (cut recipes GUI): the Recipes tab.
- #93 (spun design editor): "Edit outline" in the holder editor can open it.

## Open questions

1. Dialog or dockable window: can the user keep it open beside the viewport?
2. User-made holders need a store and a file format. Is that part of #3645?
3. Is a recipe one row for each material on the tool, as today? Or is it a shared object with a name (#3393)?
4. Does this dialog become the assembly editor of #2452?
5. Which part is the first slice? Suggestion: the dialog with the Tools list and the editor, on the data model of today. Holders and "My library" follow when their stores exist.

## Notes

- The mock-up uses the default dark theme tokens and the tool fields of `main`.
- No material of another CAM product was used.
- The pictures are mock-ups made in HTML. They are not pictures of the application.

title: A .camtools library cannot hold a form-profile mill, a blunt tapered mill, or a single-form thread mill without a pitch range

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
CamCraft at c5bb09ed13f8b63e691d3a5ed6fb0be6a64ee2aa.

## What other tool libraries store

Fusion tool libraries store three kinds of mill that a `camcraft-tools` definition has no field for:

1. Form mill: a drawn profile, a list of (radius, height) points from the axis at the tip, round the cutter and back to the axis. It covers thread mills, double-angle cutters, radius-profile cutters and any ground shape.
2. Tapered mill: a cone with a tip diameter (flat) or a corner radius (ball) at the tip, a taper angle per side and a shoulder diameter at the cutting length (tapered engravers, ball-tip tapered mills).
3. Single-form thread mill: one tooth in the profile; Fusion states no pitch range (the range is in the description text, if anywhere).

## What is missing

- `kind: taper` is a cone from a sharp apex. A tool with a tip diameter or a ball tip has no field; writing it as `taper` shifts the cone by half the tip diameter at every height.
- The drawn cutter outline (`set_tool_cutter_profile`, `ToolCutter`) exists in a project but a `.camtools` definition cannot carry it (`tool_edit` lists `cutter` as not here), so an arbitrary form profile cannot travel with the tool. `kind: form` is a lathe gauge.
- `thread_mill_single` needs `pitch` and `pitch_min`; a source that stores only the tooth has neither.
- Smaller: the dovetail check `top < sr` compares with no tolerance, so a neck that meets the flank exactly (head 6.096 mm, 1.4605 mm high, 45 degree flank, neck 3.175 mm) is refused by float dust: `3.048 - 1.4605 / tan(45 deg)` is one ulp under `1.5875`.

## Synthetic example

Form mill, mm: profile `(0,0) (2,0) (4,0.8) (2,1.6) (2,9) (4,11) (4,40) (0,40)` (one 43.6 degree V tooth on a 4 mm radius shank).
Tapered mill, mm: tip diameter 1, taper angle 30 degrees per side, cutting length 10, shoulder diameter 12.

## Ask

Any of: a `tip_d` (and ball radius) on `taper`; an optional `cutter` outline in the definition, judged by `cutter_profile::check`; an optional `pitch_min` default for `thread_mill_single`; a small tolerance in the dovetail neck check.

Until then Dutchman writes only the multi-form thread mill (rows of equal teeth at one pitch, read from the profile) and the sharp-tipped taper, and reports the others as not carried over.

## Measured

On a 97-tool Fusion library: 85 written, 12 not written (11 single-tooth form mills, 1 tapered mill with a ball tip). One multi-form thread mill and one dovetail now convert.

The push would have been rejected or would have clobbered. The local design is held and recorded on the PR.
- #3577: a max-tier rework and a text-fix worker both wrote `issue/3567-ramp-entry-at-dead-end`; the text fix pushed `4d464e006` over the rework's head while the rework's independent duplicate stayed uncommitted.
- Same class, earlier: prepared branches were pushed by the coordinating session while the worker that made them was about to push (`#3391`, `#3494`).

## Harm

- A worker spends an hour, then cannot push.
- A push race invites a force-push, which the law forbids.
- Two reviews run on two implementations of one fix.
- The status reports disagree, and the coordinator relays a head that is not ours (as happened with #3650).

## Rule

Whoever claims the issue owns the branch. One writer for one branch at one time. A second session that finds a live claim or a live writer on the branch stands down and names the live writer.

## What to change

- A branch owner record that both sessions read before a dispatch: a claim comment on the PR (or the issue) that names the writer and the base, or a small `.claude/claims/issue-N` file with the writer, the branch and the head it started from.
- The coordinator checks the PR head and the owner record before every dispatch, and writes its own record.
- A push that the remote refuses because the branch moved is a STOP with a report, never a force-push.
- The skills that dispatch (`work-issue`, `review-prs`, `resolve-conflicts`, `merge-ready`) say where the record lives.

## Related

- #3567, #3577, #3650.
- The two-session setup itself: a second session and this coordinator both write the same repository.

title: The verifier slices at every cut Z: an interpolated ramp turns 3 planes into 1,700 and minutes into hours

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Main is broken or a regression with no workaround; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

body:
The verifier slices the part at every distinct cut Z. A path with an interpolated ramp has about 1,700 cut planes instead of the 3 cut levels, and the band-reach and tangency laws then take minutes. The same path takes 89.6 s as a whole suite on main.

## Evidence

From PR #3577's head (one Waterline Outside generation, debug, temporary counters, reverted):

- The generator is fast: `ring_plan_ramped` 110 ms; each level walk 1.5 to 1.8 ms; 186 `dead_end_ramp`/`push_zig` calls are all in microseconds.
- The path is 8,850 moves and 8,553 feed moves, with 1,697 distinct feed-move Z values (the cut levels are 3: z = 12, 2, 1.5).
- The time is in the verify laws:
  - `section::tangency` 28.3 s;
  - `section::solid` 0.82 s;
  - `band_reach` plane sections and grid 1.4 s, with 5,596,906 boundary samples at a 2.75 mm cell;
  - `band_reach` verdict loop: moves 0 to 6000 in 55 ms (all skipped by the `h0 >= stock_top_z` guard), then more than 148 s without finishing for the remaining 2,850 moves; single moves take 2.8 s and 28 s, about 150k `sample_tests` per move.

The unmodified single test was killed at 120 s: 100 percent CPU, 0.1 s system time, 471 MB RSS. It is CPU-bound.

## Cause

The new dead-end entry posts a zig-zag ramp, one feed move per thinned vertex per lap (`crates/motion/src/links.rs`, `push_zig`). `Rest::new` (`crates/sim/src/verify/rest.rs:89-100`) records one cut per feed chord, keyed on `m.to.z`. The path therefore has about 1,700 distinct cut planes. `band_reach_counted` (`crates/sim/src/verify/reach.rs:47`, the plane loop at 102-110 and the verdict loop near 205-240) slices the part at every distinct cut Z, so the work is `O(feed_moves x samples)`, and samples grow with the plane count: quadratic in the number of ramp Z steps. `section::tangency` (`crates/sim/src/verify/section.rs:89-146`) pays the same per-distinct-Z cost through `rest.islands_at`.

The new planner code is ruled out: `level_order.rs`, `level_rings.rs` (`order`, `unswept`, `too_short_at`), `level_ramp_entry.rs`, `descent.rs::ramp_fallback`, `links.rs::plan_zig_capped/push_zig` and the `arc_cross` retries are all sub-millisecond to about 100 ms.

## Recommended fix

In `band_reach_counted`, build the sampled plane set from the cut LEVELS (feed moves with `|from.z - to.z| < z_tol`) plus the deepest cut, instead of every `rest.cut()` record, and pass that set to the same `islands_at` and `boundary_samples` code. For this path that is 3 to 4 planes and restores the pre-PR cost; the same plane set also removes the 28 s in `section::tangency`.

This slightly reduces wall-sample coverage for ramps between levels. The heavy lanes on a sloped or stepped fixture must show that the verdicts do not change before it merges. A lower-risk variant is to quantize the plane key and cap the sample count.

## Why #3595 did not cover it

#3595 (`9a7de3781`) made the sample lookup exact and fast. It did not reduce the number of planes, so the per-plane cost stays.

## Related

- #3577: the ramp entry that exposes this; blocked until this is fixed.
- #3588: the verifier speed work, closed by #3595.
- #3587: the slow pin as a test-speed item.

body:
A user reported this in chat on 2026-11-22.

## What happens

In the simulation, the traced stock picture shows holes in the stock. Through a hole, the user sees the viewport grid behind the stock. The holes are on the faced floor, near the tool path. When the user orbits the camera, the holes change shape. Thus the cause is in the picture, not in the stock data.

The user saw this in a local build. The exact version is not known.

## Expected

The picture shows the stock as solid where the stock has material. A pixel that the march cannot resolve does not show the background as if the stock were cut through.

## Cause (from a read of `origin/main` f35202134, not built)

- `crates/ui/src/trace.wgsl` gives each ray `MAX_STEPS = 64` steps. Each step is `phi * RELAX` (0.9).
- Near a large flat face, at a low view angle, `phi` is small. The steps become small, and the ray uses all 64 steps before a hit. The ray returns status 2 (unreadable).
- `crates/ui/src/trace/composite.wgsl` (lines 47-50) discards each pixel that is not a resolved hit. The traced picture replaces the stock slot, so nothing is drawn behind the pixel. The user sees the background.
- The comment there says that a budget bail is "never painted as material". That rule is correct. But a hole also gives a wrong picture: the stock looks cut through.

## Not affected

The Deviate verdict, the post gate and the STL export do not read the traced picture. The G-code is not affected.

## Possible fixes

1. Paint a budget bail at the last march point, with a tint that shows that it is approximate. Do not discard it.
2. Increase the step budget, or set a minimum step near a surface (for example a fraction of the cell).
3. Keep the CPU twin (`camcraft_sim::stock_sim::preview::march`) in parity. The parity test is `crates/ui/tests/trace_parity.rs`.

## Related

- #3336: stock simulation performance.
- The `machined.rs` mesh is not shown when the GPU eye traces. A separate change can show the mesh when the transport is down.

Done means: a grazing view of a faced stock floor shows no background pixels inside the stock outline. A test pins this on the CPU twin, and the GPU parity test stays green.

title: No way to open a project read-only: Save can write over a reference copy

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: claimed

labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
**What happened**

CamCraft cannot open a project read-only. Every open project saves over its own file:

- In the window, Save writes to the file that was opened (`crates/ui/src/state.rs:3436-3440` on `main` 60b19abe8).
- The MCP tool `save_project` without a path, and the script call `cam.save()`, write to the file that was opened (`crates/app/src/script/api.rs:41-52`).
- `camcraft-ui` has no read-only option. `camcraft-ui --read-only job.camproj` stops with `unknown option '--read-only'` (`crates/ui/src/cli_options.rs:192`).
- The MCP tool `open_project` takes only `path`. `open_project {"path": "job.camproj", "read_only": true}` is refused with `open_project: unknown argument "read_only"` (`crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs:115-123`).

These users need a project that opens without a risk to its file:

- a user who opens a shipped example or a tester kit to look at it;
- a person who reviews a released job;
- a team that keeps reference copies on a shared folder.

CamCraft already has this behaviour for shipped machines. The machine editor refuses Save for a shipped machine, and Save As writes a copy (`crates/app/src/machine/draft.rs:35-36`, `:229-242`, `:259`).

**Expected**

- `camcraft-ui --read-only job.camproj` opens the project read-only.
- A save over the opened file is refused on every save route: the window, MCP `save_project` and script `cam.save`. The file stays byte for byte.
- Save As to another file works, and the project is then no longer read-only.
- The title bar says that the project is read-only.
- An agent can open a project read-only with `open_project {"path": ..., "read_only": true}`.

An open SolidCraft pull request adds the same option, `solidcraft --read-only` (tangency-labs/solidcraft#20830). The same name and behaviour in both apps help users who use the two.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Copy a project file, for example a shipped example, to a folder.
2. Run `camcraft-ui --read-only <copy>.camproj`. The start stops with `unknown option '--read-only'`.
3. Run `camcraft-ui <copy>.camproj`. Change a parameter and push Save. CamCraft writes over the copy.
4. In `camcraft-cli mcp`, call `open_project {"path": "<copy>.camproj", "read_only": true}`. The call is refused: `open_project: unknown argument "read_only"`.

I found this by code inspection.

**camcraft version and OS**

`main` at 60b19abe8 (2026-11-22). Windows 11.

**Proposed change**

- A new start option `--read-only` in the option table (`cli_options.rs`). It applies to the one project file on the command line. A model file is imported as usual, because an import makes a new project with no file. A headless start ignores it.
- One rule in `crates/app/src/project/`, `project::refuse_read_only_save`, next to `project::save` and its other refusals. It refuses a save to the file that the project is open read-only from. The window's `save_project_path` and `script::api::v_save` call it. `v_save` serves MCP `save_project`, script `cam.save` and the live MCP seam of a window.
- The rule compares files, not spellings (canonical paths), because the Save As dialog gives an absolute path.
- In the window, Save on a read-only project opens the Save As dialog, as the shipped-machine editor does. A save to the opened file from the dialog is refused on the status line.
- Changes stay allowed in memory.
- MCP `open_project` gets an optional `read_only` boolean. Scripts get it through `cam.call("open_project", ...)`. The live seam still refuses `open_project`, but the window's read-only state reaches a live `save_project`.
- The title bar shows `CamCraft - job.camproj (read-only)`.
- No file-format change. `PROJECT_VERSION` does not change.

**Done means:** `camcraft-ui --read-only job.camproj` opens the project read-only and the title says so. Tests show that a save over the opened file is refused, and that the file stays byte for byte, through the window, MCP `save_project`, script `cam.save` and the live seam. Tests show that a save to another file works and ends read-only. A test shows that the option parses and keeps the file argument. The help text, `docs/user-guide/start-options.md`, the site guide and `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` describe it.

I prepared this issue with Claude Code (an AI agent) and checked it.

On one Windows machine the build step of `cargo xtask gate quick --base main` failed in 4 of 4 runs with the default job budget (16). It passed in 4 of 4 runs with `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=4`. The source did not change between the runs. This is a different fault from #3589 (the crash of the lib test process).

## What happens
Step 1 of the quick plan is `ui build (--no-run)`. Its command is:

    cargo test -j 16 -p camcraft-ui --no-run --lib --test boundary --test boundary_picks --test contour_dxf_sketch --test sinker_setup --test tap_hand --test theme_example --test theme_files --test waterjet_tool

It fails with "compile error". The first error of each failing run names a dependency crate, and it is a different crate each time:

    error[E0460]: found possibly newer version of crate `png` which `camcraft_app` depends on
    error[E0462]: found staticlib `zerocopy` instead of rlib or dylib which `camcraft_app` depends on
    error[E0786]: found invalid metadata files for crate `accesskit` which `camcraft_ui` depends on
    error[E0786]: found invalid metadata files for crate `test`

Each run then shows many errors of the form `error[E0463]: can't find crate for 'camcraft_ui'` (or `camcraft_app`). Those follow from the first error. The 8 integration suites after the failed build still ran and passed in each run.

## Conditions
- Windows 11 Home 10.0.26300, 16 logical CPUs, local disk.
- rustc 1.99.1 (58cf8f9c3 2026-10-13), cargo 1.99.1, target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.
- The gate sets `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0` for each cargo step. I set no other build variable.
- `sccache` is not installed, and `RUSTC_WRAPPER` and `CARGO_BUILD_RUSTC_WRAPPER` are not set (checked in the process, user and machine environment). So no compile cache or wrapper is in use.
- Two different branches, both based on `main` 4c0a157e1, gave the same result.
- `cargo clean -p camcraft-ui` before a run did not help.
- I started no other cargo command at the same time as these runs.

## Runs
| Run | Job budget | Build step |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 16 | fail (`png`) |
| 2 | 16 | fail (`zerocopy`) |
| 3 | 16, after `cargo clean -p camcraft-ui` | fail (`accesskit`) |
| 4 | 16, after `cargo clean -p camcraft-ui` | fail (`test`) |
| 5 | 4 (`CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=4`) | ok |
| 6 | 4 (`CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=4`) | ok |
| 7 | 4 (`CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=4`), later run on the first branch | ok |
| 8 | 4 (`CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=4`), later run on the second branch | ok |

## Questions
1. Do you see this on your Windows runner or on other machines?
2. Is the gate meant to run several `rustc` processes on the same dependency at the same time (that is what `-j 16` with 8 test targets does)? I do not know the cause. It looks like a race on the files in `target\debug\deps`.
3. Until it is understood, can the `gate` skill tell contributors to try `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=4` when this error shows?

I did not look for the cause further.

body:
## Goal

Add a pure toolpath transform module in `crates/cl/src/cl/transform.rs` (re-exported by `camcraft-app`). Toolpath patterns, mirror folders, and nesting (`#2166`) share this module.

## Scope

- **Translation (`translate`):** Shift every move, arc center, `Cycle`, `CompSpan`, `EdgeBreak`, and `PlasmaCut` by `(dx, dy, dz)`. Keep coordinates finite and snapped consistently with `crates/cl/src/cl/moves.rs` (`lattice`).
- **2D XY rigid transform (`transform_xy`):** Rotate and translate a `Toolpath` in XY by `(tx, ty, angle_deg)` around a pivot. Rotate XY arc centers, cycles, compensation spans, and edge breaks. Flatten or refuse `XZ`/`YZ` vertical arcs clearly. Nesting (`#2166`) calls this function directly.
- **3D rotary axis rotation (`rotate_about_axis`):** Rotate a `Toolpath` about an `A` (X) or `B` (Y) axis through an origin by `angle_deg`. Update `Move::axis` using `crates/cl/src/cl/frame.rs` (`TiltedFrame`) and `crates/cl/src/cl/pose.rs`. Flatten tilted arcs at `chord_tol`.
- **Vertical-plane mirror (`mirror_plane`):** Reflect a `Toolpath` across a vertical plane (`nz == 0`).
  - Refuse horizontal or tilted mirror planes by name (matching `crates/post/src/post/wcs_flip.rs`).
  - Under `GeometricMirror`, reflect all coordinates and arc centers, invert `arc.ccw` (`G2` <-> `G3`), and swap `CompSide` (`G41` <-> `G42`), matching `crates/post/src/post/invert.rs` (RS-274 / ISO 6983).
  - Under `PreserveClimb`, reverse planar cutting pass chains safely after entry and before retract (swapping lead-in and lead-out, keeping original `arc.ccw` and `CompSide`) for 2D contours, profiles, and chamfers. Refuse by name any path whose entry or engagement cannot reverse safely (helical ramps, adaptive clearing, multi-pass roughing).
- **Refusals:** Return a named `TransformError` for unsupported records (turning `ThreadCycle`, `ProbeTouch`, tilted moves under mirror, non-finite inputs). Add no new crate dependencies.

## Done means

Unit tests in `crates/cl/` verify micron-accurate translation, XY rotation, A/B axis rotation, vertical-plane mirroring (`G2`/`G3` and `G41`/`G42` swap), safe 2D contour pass reversal under `PreserveClimb`, and named refusals for unsupported records and horizontal mirror planes.

title: 3D Finish: an option to stop the waterline ring pass on steep flanks

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
## What is asked

A contributor asks for one control on 3D Finish: a switch that turns off the waterline ring pass, so the operation cuts its raster lines only. The contributor's words, quoted unchanged (chat, 2026-11-19):

> how hard would it be to make a checkbox that can disable the waterline portion?

## What the tool does today

A Parallel 3D Finish operation splits the terrain at 45 degrees. Shallow facets get the Z-following raster lines. Steep facets get waterline rings: `parallel()` runs one raster pass, then `rings_and_tail` (`crates/motion/src/finishing3d/raster.rs` line 210). The ring paths run about 90 degrees across the raster lines. Every wall that stands above the Bottom plane gets its ring ladder: hole walls, end walls, and the sloped edges of a tilted top face.

The picture below shows a contributor's test part: a long bar with a top face tilted 2 degrees and two openings, cut with a 0.3125 in ball-end, Bottom 0.300 in. The purple arrow marks one ring run that still survives on a wall near the near end. The tall ladders at the far end wall are the same law at the high end of the sloped face. The raster family cannot cover those walls; only the rings can.

![Ring run surviving on a wall at Bottom 0.300 in, parallel to the bar length and near the near end edge](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/screenshots/issue-2811-waterline-arrow.png)

## Why the switch is wanted

On a part whose steep flanks are out of scope, the rings add cutting time, and they add paths the machinist did not ask for. Some machinists want the lines only, and accept the walls as they stand. One checkbox should say that choice out loud.

## Proposed shape

- One parameter, for example `waterlines: bool`, default on. Existing behaviour does not change.
- GUI name: not just "off". The control must name the consequence, for example "Steep flanks: Waterlines / Leave uncut".
- The switch applies to the Parallel pattern. Whether Parallel multi and Scallop take it is a decision. Blend should likely never take it: its 30-45 degree double cut needs the rings to remove the staircase (its own note says so). The maintainer decides this scope.

## Laws the switch must keep

1. With the switch off and steep flanks present, the path must carry a visible note that names the uncut flanks and their count. Silent rest material is not allowed (Prime Directive).
2. A model that is fully steep with the switch off must refuse with a clear error, not post an empty program. The raster answers `false` for an all-steep model; today "the rings alone carry it".
3. The parameter round-trips in the project file. Old project files load with the default, on.
4. The 3D finish MCP parameter surface exposes the same field (same rule as `fill_openings` and `gap_link`).

## Measured support (headless probe, main `744c0847b`)

Synthetic model: bar 24 x 160 mm, flat bottom z 0, top face sloped 2 degrees, two through openings, ball 7.94 mm, Parallel, gap link Jump. The probe classifies the XY direction of every Feed move.

- Bottom 0: 188 along-wall Y-family Feed runs at Z ladder levels about 0.4 mm apart. Zero Feed runs cross the open top face. All perpendicular feed sits on walls.
- Bottom raised to 9.75 mm (near the high top edge): the same perpendicular runs collapse to three ladder levels per wall, and only over the stretch where the face still stands above Bottom. Nothing sits in the open middle.

This matches the picture: raising Bottom shrank the ring set everywhere except where walls still rise above it. The behaviour is correct as designed; this issue asks for control, not for a defect fix. The probe code can become the pinning test for the switch.

## Done means

- A checkbox flips the ring pass on and off, and each state has a motion test that pins it.
- Off plus steep flanks: a note names the uncut flanks; no ring moves appear in the CL output.
- Off plus a steep-only model: a refusal with a clear message.
- Project-file round-trip test and MCP parity pass.
- The 3D finish page shows the control with its consequence wording.

## Classification

This account is a contributor and cannot set labels. Suggested labels, for a maintainer: `enhancement`, `P6`, `effort:high` (safety floor: it changes posted G-code when the switch is used), `area:motion`, `area:ui`, `area:mcp`. The body was written by the contributor's agent at the contributor's request.

```
generate failed: could not generate the toolpath: Rotary Parallel1: invalid machining parameters: the model's normals share no rotation axis - a turned workpiece is rotary work; finish a freeform with the 5-Axis kinds
```

The refusal is correct for today's design (the rotary operations fit the axis of revolution from the mesh normals, and a helicoid has no common axis). But this part is classic **4-axis wrap work**: it is clamped in the A axis on its own centreline, A turns and the tool follows the lobes. The user has a 4-axis machine, not a 5-axis one, so the message's advice ("finish a freeform with the 5-Axis kinds") does not help.

## Wanted

1. When the model is not a solid of revolution, the rotary operations can take the axis from the setup instead: the mounted machine's rotary line (A about X) through the WCS / a stated centre (e.g. the stock's or the shaft ends' fitted axis), stated by the user, not guessed.
2. Rotary Parallel (and Rotary Offset roughing) then wrap the toolpath round that axis with the existing radial field check (gouge against the fitted skin = the model itself, stock, part), so a helical rotor, auger, fluted shaft or cam with non-turned features can be finished on 4 axes.
3. Until then, the refusal message names the 4-axis case: e.g. "the model is not a shape of revolution; rotary operations need one today (#this). A part clamped on A that is not turned (helical lobes) is not supported yet" - not only the 5-axis pointer.

## Notes

- The shaft ends of this model are turned; only the lobes are helical. The ends alone would fit an axis, so "fit the axis from the turned faces only" could be a first step.
- Safety floor: the axis must be stated or fitted from real turned faces; a guessed axis that is off by a fraction of a mm wraps a gouge. Refuse when the stated axis and the turned faces disagree.
- Clean-room: published 4-axis wrapping literature only.

body:
## What happens

`add_tool` gives each new tool the lowest unused number from 1 (camcraft-mcp skill: "Assigns the lowest unused tool number in 1-99999"). Many machines keep a fixed pocket for the probe or a tool setter:

- Tormach PathPilot machines: the probe is **T99** by convention.
- A Hurco VMX30U (WinMax): the export on #2566 has `PROBE` as **T1**.
- A FANUC Robodrill (31i-A5): the owner's **T1** is the probe.

On the last two, CamCraft's first cutting tool becomes T1, so a posted program calls the probe for a face or drill operation. Found while making the Robodrill test kit (#2603): its first version faced with T01, and the owner answered "I will not face with my probe!". The kit was renumbered to T12-T15 by hand.

## Expected

- A machine file can name reserved tool numbers, for example `"tooling": { "reserved": [ { "number": 1, "use": "probe" } ] }` (the exact key to be decided).
- `add_tool` and the tool library skip those numbers for cutting tools; a probe tool takes the probe's number.
- `set_tool_number` to a reserved number for a tool of the wrong kind is refused by name (or warned), and verify/post warn when a program calls a reserved pocket for cutting.
- The Tormach machine files reserve T99 (probe); a generic VMC reserves nothing.

## Done means

A test with a machine file that reserves T1 for the probe: the first added end mill gets T2, the probe gets T1, and a program that cuts with T1 is refused by name.

Wanted:
1. **Check:** at start (and at most once a day), read the latest release tag from GitHub (`api.github.com/repos/NeoTech/Camcraft/releases/latest`). No account, no telemetry; a setting turns it off; offline or rate-limited = silent, never an error dialog. Never in the browser (wasm) build.
2. **Show:** a small "Update available: vX.Y.Z" item at the right of the title bar, next to the version (#352). Its tooltip names the version and links the release notes.
3. **Install on click** - the hard part, because the app is running:
   - Download the asset for this platform (Windows zip/installer, macOS, Linux tar/AppImage, FreeBSD) to a temp folder and check its SHA-256 against the release (the release needs a checksum file - today it has none) before anything runs.
   - Unsaved work: ask to save first (the usual unsaved-changes prompt); never drop work.
   - Replace and restart: a running exe cannot be overwritten on Windows. Usual pattern: quit, let a small helper (or the installer itself) swap the files and start the new version; or rename the running exe aside and put the new one in place, then restart. Package-manager installs (AUR, Homebrew, a .deb) are not self-updated: show "update available" with the command to run instead.
   - Failure at any step leaves the old version working and says what failed.
4. Never auto-install without a click; never download in the background without the setting allowing it.

Done means: on Windows and one of macOS/Linux, a build that is one release behind shows "Update available", a click updates it and restarts on the new version with the project reopened; a corrupt download (bad checksum) is refused with a message and the old version still starts; with the setting off or offline, nothing is shown and nothing fails.

Add a built-in 3-axis router post for the **RichAuto DSP A11** controller in `assets/posts/richauto.cps`. Register it in `BUILTINS` in `crates/app/src/posting.rs` and pin it in `crates/app/tests/conformance.rs`.

## Context

Issue #1907 confirmed that mkinney's friend runs a **RichAuto DSP A11** handheld controller. Common Laguna Swift (`4x4`, `4x8`, `5x10`) and Grizzly CNC routers (`G0894`, `G0931`, `G0895`) also use this controller.

CamCraft's existing posts (`assets/posts/grblhal.cps`, `fanuc.cps`, `carvera.cps`, `tinyg.cps`) do not run safely on a RichAuto A11:
- `grblhal.cps` emits `G91.1`, `G94`, `G53 G0 Z...`, `T<n> M6`, and canned cycles. RichAuto A11 uses the pendant `AbsCntr` menu switch (`Off` = incremental) instead of `G91.1`, and basic router firmware can reject canned cycles or `G91.1`.
- `fanuc.cps` emits `%`, `O0001`, `T.. M6`, `G43 H..`, `G49`, `G91 G28 Z0`, and `G84` tapping.

## Specification (OEM manuals only)

1. **Units and file format:** default to `mm` (`G21`) to match RichAuto's internal metric math and avoid `G20` scale errors. Write `.nc` ASCII files with parentheses comments `(...)`. Omit `%`, `O` program numbers, and `;` comments.
2. **Preamble and arcs:** write `G21`, `G90`, `G17`, `G40`, and `G80`. Omit `G91.1`, `G94`, `G43`, and `G49`. Emit incremental `I`/`J`/`K` matching `AbsCntr = Off`. Handle `G54` cleanly (`G54` default or document `Read G54` vs `Ign G54` in post notes; handle or refuse multi-WCS safely).
3. **Spindle and warm-up:** write `S<rpm> M3`. Add a configurable spindle dwell property (`G04 P<ms>`, default `0`) so the post works alongside the pendant `Spindle Delay` setting. Document 8-step `S1`-`S8` VFD wiring in post comments.
4. **Drilling and tool changes:** expand all canned drill cycles (`G81`, `G82`, `G83`, `G73`, `G86`, `G89`) to plain `G0`/`G1` moves (using the pattern in `assets/posts/carvera.cps` and `tinyg.cps`). Refuse mid-program tool changes on the initial 3-axis manual slice (or lift Z cleanly and write `M0` with `(CHANGE TOOL T<n>)` rather than bare `T<n> M6`).
5. **Refusals and footer:** refuse `G84` tapping, `G41`/`G42` cutter compensation, and probing. Retract Z to clearance height in work coordinates, stop spindle (`M5`) and coolant (`M9` if active), and end with `M30` (no trailing `%`).

## Rules

- Clean room: use only RichAuto DSP A11 OEM documentation, RS-274 / ISO 6983 standards, and CamCraft repository patterns (`assets/posts/AGENTS.md`). Do not read or copy Autodesk, HSMWorks, or third-party CAM posts.

## Done means

- `assets/posts/richauto.cps` exists and registers in `BUILTINS` in `crates/app/src/posting.rs`.
- `crates/app/tests/conformance.rs` passes for `RichAuto DSP A11` across all mill goldens and refuses `G84`, `G41`/`G42`, and probing by name.
- Posted `.nc` output uses `G21`, incremental `I`/`J`, expanded drilling moves, `(...)` comments, safe Z retract, and `M30` with no `%`, `O` headers, `G91.1`, `G43`, or `G49`.
- Decision entry added under `docs/decisions/`.

body:
### What are you trying to do

Open CamCraft on a Mac after downloading it from the releases page, without having to override Gatekeeper.

The macOS app is ad-hoc signed and not notarized (`scripts/package-macos.sh`: "Distribution signing and notarization can replace this when credentials exist"). A browser download gets the quarantine flag, and macOS then blocks the first launch because Apple can't verify the developer. Every new release is a new copy, so a user has to override Gatekeeper again after each update.

The README says the first launch "may require Control-click → Open". Since macOS 15 (Sequoia) that no longer works for an app that isn't notarized: the user has to try to open it, then go to System Settings › Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway, or run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/CamCraft.app` in Terminal.

### How you imagine it working

The release signs the macOS app with a Developer ID certificate and notarizes it, so it opens like any other downloaded app. It would work the same way Windows signing does now (`scripts/sign.ps1`):

- `scripts/package-macos.sh` signs with Developer ID (hardened runtime, secure timestamp) when signing credentials are configured through the environment, and keeps today's ad-hoc signature, with a printed "unsigned" line, when they aren't. Unsigned stays a valid release.
- When credentials are configured, the release job submits the ZIP or DMG with `xcrun notarytool submit --wait`, then staples the ticket to the app and the DMG with `xcrun stapler staple`.
- The certificate and the notary credentials (an App Store Connect API key, or an Apple ID with an app-specific password) live in repository secrets, as the Windows PFX does.

This needs an Apple Developer Program membership, so whether and when to do it is the maintainer's call. A smaller step that helps meanwhile: update the README's macOS line to the macOS 15 steps above.

body:
Asked for by the maintainer (2026-11-13, in chat), after a feature comparison with the open-source project stevecad/camlib: "We wanna cover some of the toolpaths and things like that at first." and, on the suggested picks: "Lets create issues on your suggestions, they made sense." On sources: "We should use perplexity to find literature on those types of toolpaths and not copy them straight up".

What is missing: rest machining exists for 3D operations, but a 2D Pocket (and 2D Adaptive) cannot be limited to what a larger previous tool left: a small finishing tool re-cuts the whole pocket in air.

Wanted: on 2D Pocket and 2D Adaptive, a "Rest machining" group: on/off, source (previous tool diameter and corner radius entered by hand, or "from the previous operations" using the carried stock), and a rest allowance. The path covers only the regions the previous tool could not reach (corners, narrow necks), entered from already cut space where there is any.

Safety: the rest region must be a superset of the material really left. Under-reading it leaves a full-width cut for a small tool, which breaks it. With the hand-entered source the op says in its summary that it trusts the entered tool; with the carried-stock source the regions are checked against the stock simulation in a test.

Sources: step one of the work is a literature search (Perplexity) for published material on 2D rest-region computation (offset differences, medial-axis reach of a tool); the code is written from that and named in the provenance comment. camlib is a feature list only: no code is copied or adapted from it.

Done means: a pocket with 3 mm corners roughed by a 12 mm tool gets a rest pass with a 4 mm tool that cuts only the corners (golden CL); simulation shows no passes over cleared floor and no plunge into uncut stock; undo/redo; MCP parameters; a previous tool smaller than the current one is refused by name; the literature used is cited in the PR.

title: Process changes - fork maintainers please subscribe

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: P?
labels.description: Paused: never picked until the maintainer sets a real priority

body:
**Subscribe to this issue** (the "Subscribe" button on the right) if you work from a fork of CamCraft, especially with an AI agent.

Forks sync product code only at release tags (AGENTS.md "A fork syncs from upstream at each cut tag"). But the *process* - `AGENTS.md`, the agent definitions in `.claude/agents/`, the skills in `.claude/skills/` and `scripts/gate.*` - changes between releases, and a fork's agents should follow the current rules (review labels, priority labels, release steps, and so on).

**How it works:**
- `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` holds one number. Every PR that changes a process file bumps it.
- Every such PR also adds a comment **here**: the new version, what changed, and what to pull. Subscribers get one notification per change.
- A fork's agent compares its `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` with upstream's at the start of each session and, if upstream is newer, pulls just the process files (AGENTS.md "Process files sync on every session"). Product code still waits for the next release tag.

**To pull by hand:**
```
git fetch upstream
git checkout upstream/main -- AGENTS.md .claude/agents .claude/skills .claude/PROCESS_VERSION scripts/gate.ps1 scripts/gate.sh
git commit -m "chore(process): sync process files to upstream PROCESS_VERSION <n>"
```

This issue stays open and pinned. It's labelled `P?` so no agent ever picks it up as work.
